To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
increased expression of the large subunit gene for calcium-activated neutral peptidase II in cardiomyocytes is responsible for enhanced enzymatic activity in hypertensive rats.
increased enzymatic activity of CANP II in cardiac tissue of hypertensive rats is associated with enhanced expression of CANp II mRNA.

the levels of CAN P II large subunit gene mRNA are increased in cardiomyocytes from 2K-1C hypertensive rats, but not in SHR cardiomyocytes, suggesting that the enhanced activity of the enzyme is not a consequence of increased expression of its gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new mechanism of gene regulation in hypertensive cardiomyocytes.
the transcriptional regulation of CANP II in cardiomyocytes from hypertensive animals.
the regulation of CANP II gene expression in hypertensive rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the increase in CANP II mRNA is a consequence of increased transcriptional activity of the gene in the hypertrophied hearts of renal hypertensives.
CANP II gene expression in the heart is increased in 2 kidney, one clip hypertension but not in the spontaneously hypertensive rats.
the enhanced activity of CANP II in 2K 1C- hypertensive rat heart is associated with an increased transcriptional activity of the CANP II large mRNA subunit gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the increased levels of mRNA for the large subunits of CANP in cardiomyocytes from 2K-1C rats are regulated at the transcription level, whereas in SHR the increased levels are due to an increased rate of transcription of the mRNA for the small subunits.
increased levels of CANP mRNA and protein in cardiomyocytes from 2K-1C hypertensive rats may contribute to increased Ca2+-dependent proteolysis in the heart of this model.
the increased expression of the calcium-activated neutral proteinase II gene is regulated at the transcription level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of CANP in hypertensive hearts is increased, which is associated with the increased enzymatic activity of the proteolytic enzyme.
CANP II gene expression is regulated in a hypertensive state and this may be an important factor in the development of cardiac hypertrophy.
CANP II gene expression is regulated at the transcription level in cardiomyocytes from the hearts of 2K-1C hypertensive rats.
